question: The former lobbyist Frédéric Baldan brought legal action against the President of the European Commission in connection with Pfizergate. In October 2025, he reported that his bank accounts with ING and Nagelmackers had been terminated1. According to Baldan, this concerned not only his own personal bank account, but also those of his consulting firm and household, as well as his five-year-old son’s savings account.

This development raises questions as to possible links between the legal dispute and the action taken by the financial institutions. Does the Council have any evidence suggesting that the closure of the bank accounts is linked to Frédéric Baldan’s Pfizergate-related activities?
answer: The Council has not discussed this question, as it does not fall within its sphere of competence.
